cover.headline: India's best consumer franchise, priced for it: FY27 growth is half price, and the multiple already assumes decades of compounding
cover.lead: Pidilite owns Fevicol, Dr. Fixit, M-Seal and Fevikwik, sells through ~5,700 distributors and lakhs of small dealers, and earns a 31% ROCE with net cash. Volumes are strong: underlying volume growth (UVG) was 11.1% in FY26 and 11.3% in Q1FY27, even after price rises of up to 12-15% to cover a spike in vinyl acetate monomer (VAM) during the West Asia conflict. But Q1FY27's 21% revenue growth was about half price, VAM has since halved from its peak, management expects to pass some price back, and FY26's 24% EBITDA margin was already the top of its own 20-24% corridor. The street values Pidilite on **P/E (50x FY28E or Jun-28E EPS)**. We forecast EPS of ₹27.8 in FY27E and ₹31.6 in FY28E, close to the street for FY27 and ~5% below for FY28. Applying **45x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹33.7** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,509, DCF ₹866. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A genuine moat in the core
arguments.p: Fevicol is "synonymous with adhesives" (CRISIL); competitors copy Pidilite's price moves "almost to a T" (MD). C&B UVG was 12.2% in Q1FY27 on top of the price rises. Consolidated C&B segment EBITDA margin was 33.0% in FY26 and ROE 24.0%, with capex of only 3-5% of revenue.

arguments.h: FY27 growth is flattered by price
arguments.p: Q1FY27 standalone revenue +22.2% = UVG 11.3% plus ~10% price and mix. VAM was consumed at US$1,370/t in Q1 (US$924 a year earlier) and fell ~50% from its peak by August; management talks of rebates. We forecast revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}} in FY27E, then +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}} as price laps.

arguments.h: Margins are at the top of the range
arguments.p: EBITDA margin was 17% in FY23 when inputs spiked and 24.1% in FY26 on cheap ones; Q1FY27 26.3% included low-cost inventory that "will unravel in the second quarter" (CFO). We model {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}: no further expansion.

At ₹1,465 the stock trades at 52.7x our FY27E and 46.4x FY28E EPS. Its 64x median forward P/E since 2021 has de-rated with consumer peers; our 45x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}. A DCF at an 11.3% cost of equity gives only ₹866: even 15 years of double-digit growth does not support today's price at that discount rate.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much margin the high-cost VAM inventory takes in the quarter, and whether rebates start.
VAM and crude prices: a lasting fall supports margins but brings price give-backs; a renewed spike hits margins again.
UVG through FY27: management wants double digit and "about 100 bps" a year of improvement; watch for demand compression from industry-wide price rises.
Competition in tile adhesives (cement and tile makers entering) and waterproofing; the export recovery in B2B.
Use of ₹4,200 cr of net cash: pioneering categories, partnerships or acquisitions.

sections.title: Glue, waterproofing and tile fixing: a brand house sold through India's tradesmen

blocks.p: Pidilite makes the products India's carpenters, plumbers, masons, painters and households use to stick, seal and waterproof. Its **Consumer & Bazaar (C&B)** segment (81.6% of FY26 standalone sales) sells branded adhesives and sealants (Fevicol, Fevikwik, Fevistik, M-Seal, Araldite), construction and paint chemicals (Dr. Fixit waterproofing, Roff tile adhesives and grouts) and art and craft materials (Fevicryl). "Bazaar" means sales through dealers to tradesmen rather than to households. Its **Business to Business (B2B)** segment (18%) sells industrial adhesives, resins, construction chemicals for projects and organic pigments to other companies. Management sorts the portfolio into **core** (established brands growing at 1-2x real GDP), **growth** (waterproofing, tile adhesives, projects, joineries: 2-4x GDP) and **pioneer** categories (new bets such as Unofin renders, Haisha paints and electronics adhesives), with core and the rest "nearly 50-50".

sections.title: Under-penetrated categories, a volatile input-cost cycle and more competition

blocks.p: Pidilite's categories grow with home building, renovation and furniture making, and with the shift from crude methods (cement to fix tiles, no waterproofing) to branded chemicals. That shift has a long way to run: management puts tile-adhesive penetration at 20-30% of the ~₹6,500 cr tile & stone market, and waterproofing in small builders' projects is still "not being done". Demand was strong into 2026: urban demand turned "buoyant" in Jan-Mar 2026 after the GST 2.0 rate cuts and income-tax relief, in the MD's view.

The cost side is a petrochemical cycle. Pidilite's key inputs (VAM, polymers, acrylates, resins) follow crude oil and supply shocks. Raw and packaging materials were ~45% of sales in FY26 (CRISIL). The West Asia conflict that started in early 2026 pushed the weighted raw-material basket up 40-50% at the peak; VAM more than doubled. Pidilite and its rivals raised prices together, and by August VAM had fallen back about half way. The other change is competition: paint majors are pushing into waterproofing (and one has built its own VAM/VAE plant), and cement and tile makers are entering tile adhesives.

sections.title: Consumer & Bazaar: the moat, now growing on price as well as volume

pair.title: C&B revenue by quarter (standalone)
pair.source: Company presentations (Q2FY26 derived from 9M less Q1 and Q3)

pair.title: C&B volume growth stepped up from 6-8% to 9-15%

bullets: **What it is.** Branded adhesives, sealants, waterproofing, tile adhesives and art materials sold through dealers to tradesmen and households: ₹11,505 cr of consolidated net revenue in FY26 (79% of the group), growing ~15% a year since FY21.

**Margins track inputs.** Consolidated C&B segment EBITDA margin: FY21 32.5%, FY22 26.6%, FY23 23.4%, FY24 29.0%, FY25 30.9%, FY26 33.0%. The FY23 trough came when VAM and other inputs spiked; FY26 is a record.

**FY26-Q1FY27 acceleration.** C&B UVG rose from 7.2% in FY25 to 11.1% in FY26 and 12.2% in Q1FY27. Management credits urban buoyancy, more field marketing (standalone A&SP +19% in FY26, +37% in Q1FY27) and share gains in growth categories, and says it did not load the channel in March.

**Pricing.** Fevicol prices rose ~5% in April and another 7-9% in May 2026 (12-15% in all); company-wide ~4-5% plus ~7-8%. Rivals followed. With VAM falling, management expects to give some back through rebates, "particularly in our Bazaar business".

**Competition.** Pidilite is the leader in consumer adhesives; in tile adhesives the top 4-5 players hold 80-90%, and cement and tile makers are entering; Pidilite answers with more plants (Nio Pro now made in four), quality and "total delivered cost".

blocks.callout: **Our view:** C&B is the best part of Pidilite and the reason it deserves a premium. We model C&B revenue {{as.segments.0.growth.0|chg}} in FY27E (UVG ~10.5% plus ~7.5% price after rebates), then +11% and +12%, with segment EBITDA margin of 32.2-32.4%, a little below FY26's 33.0%. The risk is not volume; it is that margins revert toward the 23-29% of FY22-24 if input costs spike again.

sections.title: B2B: projects are growing, pigment exports are not, and there is no moat

pair.title: B2B revenue by quarter (standalone)
B2B volume growth fell as exports shrank
pair.source: Company presentations (export UVG disclosed from Q3FY26)

bullets: **What it is.** Industrial adhesives, resins, project construction chemicals and organic pigments: ₹3,036 cr of consolidated net revenue in FY26. CRISIL calls it "a bulk commodity business"; segment EBITDA margin has ranged from 10.8% (FY21) to 20.6% (FY25).

**Two halves.** Domestic B2B (Pidilite Professional Solutions selling waterproofing and construction systems to builders, metros, hotels and data centres; industrial adhesives for packaging, footwear, joineries) grew UVG 15.6%, 21.5% and 10.4% in the last three quarters. Exports (mainly pigments) fell each quarter, hit by the West Asia conflict from March 2026.

**Subsidiaries.** Domestic B2B subsidiaries (incl. Nina Percept, waterproofing contracting) shrank 5% in FY26 to ₹359 cr; Nina's order book is "very, very healthy" but sites were shut by pollution curbs.

blocks.callout: B2B is a useful second leg (its revenue more than doubled since FY21) but it does not carry the brand premium. We model revenue {{as.segments.1.growth.0|chg}} in FY27E and +10-11% after, with segment EBITDA margin of 19.5-20%, close to FY25-26 and well above the 10-13% of FY21-23.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (company filings, calls and CRISIL to Sep-2026)

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Pidilite has one of the widest moats in Indian consumer goods. Fevicol's brand, the relationship with millions of carpenters and other tradesmen, and a dealer network that reaches 40,000+ towns let it lead price moves and grow volumes 10%+ a year in a category it created. The moat protects **share and volume**, not the **gross margin**: Pidilite has no captive raw materials, so a VAM spike hits profit until prices catch up (FY22-23, early FY27). In the growth categories (tile adhesives, waterproofing) Pidilite is the leader but faces well-funded new entrants, and B2B has no moat at all. Net: a premium franchise, but not one whose margins can only go up.

sections.title: Ten years of steady compounding, with two input-cost dips

blocks.p: Pidilite's revenue grew from ₹5,361 cr in FY16 to ₹14,601 cr in FY26, about 10.5% a year, and net profit from ₹807 cr to ₹2,471 cr, about 12% a year. The path was not smooth. Revenue was flat in FY20-21 (slowdown, then Covid), then jumped 36% in FY22 as demand came back and the Araldite business (bought from Huntsman in Nov-2020) was added. Profit lagged in FY22-23 because raw-material costs spiked: gross margin fell from 54% to 43% and EBITDA margin to 17%. As input costs fell in FY24-26, margins recovered to a record 24% and EPS grew 36%, 20% and 18%.

pair.title: Revenue: 10.5% a year for ten years
Net profit: flat in FY20-23, then up 92% in three years
Gross margin swings with VAM and other inputs
EBITDA margin: 17% at the FY23 trough, 24% now

blocks.callout: **Our view:** volume growth is the engine and it has been reliable (underlying volume growth of ~9-11% a year in FY25-26). The swing factor is the gross margin: Pidilite buys vinyl acetate monomer (VAM) and other petrochemicals at market prices and passes cost changes on with a lag. FY26's 24% EBITDA margin is the top of management's own 20-24% corridor, earned on cheap inputs. We do not assume it keeps rising.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** Pidilite's guidance is a corridor, not a number, and its record is good: FY26 UVG of 11.1% and a 24% margin both met or beat what was said. The open question for FY27 is not demand but how much of the ~10% price stays once VAM has halved. We assume about three-quarters of it does for the year.

sections.title: A capital-light franchise: returns above 30%, cash piling up

blocks.p: Pidilite needs little capital. Over FY15-26 it generated ₹16,918 cr of operating cash, spent ₹4,554 cr on capex (about 3-4% of revenue) and paid ₹5,918 cr of dividends. The one big acquisition, Huntsman's Indian Araldite business (Nov-2020), added about ₹2,800 cr to the gross block and is the main reason ROCE fell from 33% in FY20 to 24-25% in FY22-23 (input-cost inflation did the rest). Returns have since recovered: ROCE was 31% and ROE 24% in FY26, against a cost of equity near 11%. Cash and investments rose to ₹4,649 cr at Mar-2026.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** with capex at 3-5% of revenue (management) and a 50% payout, Pidilite will keep adding ~₹1,000-1,400 cr of net cash a year on our forecasts. Management talks of "pioneering" uses (electronics adhesives, paints, Unofin) and of partnerships, not of buybacks. Large acquisitions have been rare and mostly in its own categories; a big diversifying deal is the main capital-allocation risk.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean, cash-backed and simple

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 114% of net profit in FY26, 109% in FY25 and 156% in FY24; over FY15-26 cash from operations (₹16,918 cr) exceeded net profit (₹15,136 cr).

**Few one-offs.** Exceptional items were −₹14 cr in FY26, −₹25 cr in FY25 and −₹72 cr in FY24. FY26 costs include a ₹80 cr New Labour Code charge (consolidated), so the underlying FY26 margin was ~0.5pp higher; Q4FY26 staff costs were helped by reversing a ~₹20 cr discretionary-benefit provision.
**Other income is small.** ₹248 cr in FY26, 7% of pre-tax profit; it fell in Q4FY26 on mark-to-market losses on bonds and rebounded in Q1FY27.

**Revenue recognition.** The auditor's key audit matter is revenue measured net of trade discounts and schemes (variable consideration) - the line that will move if Pidilite passes back price through rebates.

**Related party.** Purchases from Vinyl Chemicals (India), an associate with promoter director A B Parekh on its board, were ₹558 cr in FY26 (₹570 cr in FY25). Disclosed every year; we cannot test the pricing.
**Disclosure.** Good on segments (annual allocable depreciation) and volumes (UVG every quarter); no brand-level revenue or tonnage; quarterly segment data in the decks are standalone only.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit (B S R & Co. LLP), strong cash conversion, minor one-offs and a simple balance sheet. The things to watch are scheme and rebate accounting as prices fall back, and the size of related-party purchases.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹4,200 cr and suppliers fund most of the working capital

blocks.p: Pidilite has almost no debt: ₹417 cr of borrowings (mostly leases and subsidiaries' lines) at Mar-2026 against ₹4,649 cr of cash and investments; CRISIL counts an unencumbered surplus of over ₹3,920 cr and rates it AAA. Working capital is tight: inventory of ~98 days and receivables of ~55 days are largely funded by ~86 days of payables, so net working-capital days were only ~18 in FY26. Receivable days did rise from 50 to 55 in FY26, and in May-2026 the CFO said Pidilite was carrying "much higher than normal covers" of critical raw materials such as VAM, so inventory is likely to run higher during FY27.

sections.title: The street: mostly positive, with targets bunched around ₹1,700-1,900

blocks.p: Four houses published after Q1FY27 (Aug-Sep 2026): Prabhudas Lilladher Accumulate ₹1,739 (downgraded from Buy), Motilal Oswal Neutral ₹1,700, Jefferies Hold ₹1,730 and Axis Capital Buy ₹1,800, an average of ~₹1,742. In July HSBC initiated at Buy (₹1,890) and Macquarie kept Sell (₹1,350). Older calls from May still standing include Goldman Sachs Buy ₹1,700 and BofA Underperform ₹1,475. A consensus of 21 analysts on 7-Aug-26 had an average target of ₹1,741 (range ₹1,400-2,065) and FY27E EPS of ₹28.2, up from ₹26.3 before the results. The two notes with a method both use **50x P/E** on FY28E or Jun-28E earnings. Bulls focus on volume acceleration and growth categories; bears and neutrals on peak margins and valuation.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Pidilite Industries (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven revenue on the company's two reported segments, Consumer & Bazaar (C&B) and Business to Business (B2B), plus 'Others' (raw-material sales, NBFC), each on net revenue after inter-segment sales so that the three sum to reported revenue. Segment margin = segment EBITDA (segment result + allocable depreciation, consolidated segment note) as % of net revenue. Corporate costs not allocated to segments (unallocable expenses net of unallocable depreciation, as reconciled to Screener EBITDA) are a separate line. Treasury income = yield × opening cash and investments less borrowings. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Consumer & Bazaar
segments._why: FY27 +18%: Q1 standalone C&B revenue +22.5% (UVG 12.2%, i.e. ~10% from price and mix after blended price rises of ~4-5% in mid-April and ~7-8% in early May 2026). Price stays in the base until Apr-May 2027, but management expects to pass back some of it as rebates because VAM fell sharply from its ~US$1,800-2,000/t peak; we assume UVG ~10.5% plus ~7.5% price for the year (Q2 high-teens, H2 low-teens). FY28 +11%: price laps and turns slightly negative; UVG ~11% (management: double-digit UVG, 'about 100 bps' of yearly improvement is the aim, FY26 11.1%). FY29 +12%: UVG ~11% plus ~1% price.
segments._marginWhy: Consolidated C&B segment EBITDA margin was 29.1% (FY24), 30.9% (FY25) and 33.0% (FY26) on benign input costs. Q1FY27 standalone C&B PBIT margin rose 211bp YoY (low-cost inventory, proactive pricing, lower schemes), but management said Q2 would absorb high-cost inventory and some price would be passed back. We take 32.2% in FY27 and 32.4% in FY28-29: a little below FY26 and well above the FY22-23 inflation years (26.6%/23.4%).

segments.name: Business to Business
segments._why: FY27 +12%: Q1 standalone B2B revenue +16.0% (UVG 7.3%: domestic projects/industrial UVG +10.4%, exports UVG −8.4% on West Asia disruption); domestic B2B subsidiaries (Nina waterproofing etc.) grew only 3.4%. We assume exports stay weak through FY27. FY28 +10% / FY29 +11%: domestic projects (Pidilite Professional Solutions) and industrial adhesives grow double digit; exports recover partly.
segments._marginWhy: Consolidated B2B segment EBITDA margin 17.0% (FY24), 20.6% (FY25), 20.1% (FY26); 9.9-12.7% in FY22-23 when input costs spiked. Pigment exports are the most cyclical part. 19.5% in FY27 (input costs, weak exports), 20% after.

segments.name: Others (raw-material sales, NBFC)
segments._why: Small and erratic (₹39-102 cr a year since FY21); held flat.
segments._marginWhy: Segment result between −₹9 cr and +₹6 cr in FY21-26; held at zero.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Corporate costs not allocated to segments (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less reported (Screener) EBITDA: ₹353 cr (FY21, 4.8% of revenue), ₹583 cr (FY24, 4.7%), ₹750 cr (FY25, 5.7%), ₹871 cr (FY26, 6.0%). It is mostly corporate overheads, central brand/A&P and new-category costs (paints, electronics, Unofin). We hold it at ~6.0% of revenue: ₹1,020 / 1,130 / 1,260 cr.
assumptions._capexWhy: Management: capex runs at 3-5% of revenue (8-May-2026 call); FY26 ~₹570 cr per management (₹593 cr on Screener's cash flow), FY25 ₹452 cr. CRISIL (2-Sep-2026) expects ₹750-850 cr a year over the medium term (new white-glue plant in West India commissioning in Q1FY27, tile-adhesive and construction-chemical plants, automation). ₹750 / 800 / 850 cr ≈ 4.4% / 4.2% / 4.0% of revenue.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹395 cr ≈ 4.8% of average gross block (₹8,165 cr, which includes the Araldite brand and other acquired intangibles); Q1FY27 ₹97 cr (₹388 cr annualised).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and investments less borrowings (₹3,433 cr at Mar-25, ₹4,232 cr at Mar-26 on Screener). FY26 other income ₹248 cr incl. −₹18 cr exceptional = ~7.7% of opening net cash before exceptionals; Q4FY26 was hit by mark-to-market losses as bond yields rose, Q1FY27 ₹95 cr before a +₹14 cr exceptional. 7% a year.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (mainly leases and subsidiaries' working-capital lines)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹54 cr; Q1FY27 ₹13 cr. Standalone is debt free (CRISIL); ₹417 cr of borrowings incl. leases at Mar-26.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective rate 25.6% (₹849 cr on ₹3,320 cr PBT, AR note 46); Q1FY27 ~26%. 25.5% (new regime 25.2% plus non-deductibles).
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 regular dividend ₹11.50 a share (48.9% of profit before exceptionals per the company) plus a one-off special ₹5 (B K Parekh centenary); 45-49% in FY23-25. 50% ahead.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, branded consumer franchise with steady volumes; below-market sensitivity (Ke 11.3%).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; a dominant domestic brand franchise can grow near nominal GDP for long, but we stay at the top of the house 5-6% range: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~12% to 9% by year 15: underpenetrated waterproofing and tile adhesives keep growth above GDP for a decade, core adhesives grow at 1-2x real GDP.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: From ~24% towards 23%, the upper half of management's 20-24% corridor: input-cost cycles recur.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~4% of revenue towards 3.5%, within management's 3-5% band.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Price rises stick while VAM falls back (no rebates), UVG runs at 12-13% as urban demand stays buoyant and waterproofing/tile adhesives take share; exports recover in FY28; C&B margin holds near 34% and consolidated EBITDA margin settles around 25%, above the top of management's corridor.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Price give-backs come faster than input relief, inflation compresses demand (UVG falls to 7-8%), competition from cement and tile makers in tile adhesives and from Asian Paints/JSW in waterproofing intensifies, exports stay weak; C&B margin slips towards 30% and consolidated EBITDA margin to ~21.5%, the middle of the corridor.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Pidilite (Motilal Oswal 50x FY28E EPS, Prabhudas Lilladher 50x Jun-28E EPS, Aug-2026). 45x = Pidilite's ~64x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, cut by the ~27% median de-rating of six consumer and building-material peers versus their five-year median P/E by 30-Sep-2026 (≈47x), and by ~4% more because our FY26-29E EPS growth (~14% a year) is below the ~17% of FY21-26 and comes off peak-range margins. Bull 55x (its 25th-percentile forward P/E since 2021), bear 40x (its 10th percentile since 2016).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 31x Sep-28E EBITDA = Pidilite's ~56x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, less the same ~27% sector de-rating (≈41x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~27% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (≈32x), less the same ~4% growth discount.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
